title: Buying a Vacation Home in Myrtle Beach: Which Loan Fits?
description: Buying a vacation home in Myrtle Beach? Second home vs investment property loans, renting it out, Horry County property taxes and local rental rules.
h1: Myrtle Beach Vacation Home: Second Home or Investment Property Loan?
dek: Buying a beach place you'll use and rent out sometimes? Here's how lenders decide, and what Horry County taxes will look like.

about.name: Second home and investment property mortgages

faq.q: Can I rent out my Myrtle Beach second home?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you stay there part of the year, keep control of the bookings, and don't use the rent to qualify for the loan. Short-term stays in the City of Myrtle Beach collect about 13% in lodging taxes.

faq.q: How many days do you have to live in a second home?
faq.a: Fannie Mae's second home rule doesn't set a number of days. You must live there for some part of the year, and the home must be livable year-round. The two-week figure people often hear is an IRS tax rule about personal use of a rental, not a mortgage rule. Ask your tax advisor about that one.

faq.q: Can I use rental income to qualify for a second home?
faq.a: No. If you need the rent to qualify, the loan is an investment property loan. A DSCR loan, which qualifies you on the rent, is one option.

faq.q: Are property taxes higher on a second home in Myrtle Beach?
faq.a: Yes. A second home or rental in unincorporated Horry County pays about 3.3 times what an owner-occupant pays on the same house, and about 4.3 times inside the City of Myrtle Beach, at 2025 and 2026 tax rates. Your main home gets a 4% assessment and an exemption from school operating taxes that a second home doesn't.
